tldr: LLaMAR is an LM-based cognitive architecture using a plan-act-correct-verify framework for long-horizon multi-agent planning in partially observable environments, achieving state-of-the-art results without relying on oracles or simulators.
contributions: LLaMAR: An LM-based long-horizon planner for multi-agent robotics that operates iteratively without prior environmental knowledge or oracle feedback
MAP-THOR: A benchmark suite of household tasks within the AI2-THOR simulator under partial observability to standardize evaluation of multi-agent planning
Semantics-guided exploration strategy using CLIP embeddings to guide agents in unexplored environments
methods: LLaMAR employs four specialized LM modules operating iteratively at each high-level decision step: a Planner that decomposes tasks into subtasks, an Actor that selects high-level actions for each agent, a Corrector that identifies and corrects execution failures with reasoning, and a Verifier that self-verifies subtask completion from image observations. Low-level primitive actions are handled by pre-trained RL, behavior cloning, or heuristic policies. A semantically-guided exploration strategy uses CLIP image and text embeddings to determine exploration directions when agents cannot locate task-relevant objects.
results: LLaMAR achieves a 30% higher success rate than other state-of-the-art LM-based multi-agent planners in MAP-THOR and Search & Rescue tasks. It outperforms methods like SmartLLM, Two-Step, CoELA, and S-ATLAS, particularly on complex, multi-room household tasks and SAR scenarios with partial observability.
limitations: Experiments are conducted only in the AI2-THOR simulator and have not been validated in real-world robotic environments. The approach requires pre-trained low-level primitive action policies (via RL, behavior cloning, or heuristics). Multiple LMs (Planner, Actor, Corrector, Verifier) increase computational overhead compared to single-LM approaches.
